quest.title: The Answer of the Lotus Leaves and Forest
quest.description: The champion paper frog Faurobert and Princess Cimest of the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells seem to be in a... slightly odd predicament.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: You are here, my loyal Paladin. The gifts that I have prepared for you are in the chest next to us — please, take them.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What will you do next?

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Hmm... Well, first of all, I shall announce to the whole forest that the relic has made its decision.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: As for the chosen Guardian... I will tell them that it was Mr. Faurobert, the one who came from afar.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!? Why would you do that?

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Trying to explain everything we've been through would be far too complicated.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Besides, it would take too long for them to grasp the concept of me being both a princess and a Guardian at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: When the time is right, I will make a detailed record of all that happened and then inform my people in writing.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: But until then, I will still preside over all the affairs of the forest as "Princess."

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Once those "trial grounds" have been officially converted into "training grounds," I will set off.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: I still don't have the answers though.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Why did we need to wait for a Guardian, why did all those kingdoms decline as a result, and why is Rainsong Pond's calling what it is...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: There are still so many unanswered questions, so many unfinished stories.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Speaking of which, *sigh*... I have another question...

choices.text: You're not wriggling out this time!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: No, no, that's not it! Umm, Your Highness... Is there any way of knowing who the relic actually lit up for?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Hmm? Who it actually lit up for?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Yes, as we were both next to it at the time. Of course, Your Highness fully deserves to be acknowledged, but I on the other hand... I...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're a champion who's been acknowledged by a champion.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly, and that champion came specifically to ask for your help! How could you possibly still think you're unworthy?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: *sigh* Maybe it's simply that Her Highness shines so brightly that you were all mistaken...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Well then, Mr. Champion, would you be willing to undergo another trial?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: I, Princess Cimest of the Forest, shall personally bear witness to your deeds with this relic.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Of course! I do, I do, I do!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He gets so excited whenever he hears the princess's name. Hehe, Faurobert...

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Don't get me wrong! I—I'm doing this to fulfill the calling of Rainsong Pond! All that training I did, it was all to save... Uhh, I mean, protect Her Highness.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: And it's such an important task, so naturally I must ensure that it all goes without a hitch...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Are you willing to travel together with Her Highness?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I—I am...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Hehe, that's good to hear. Well then, Mr. "Champion" Faurobert, are you ready for my trial?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I am, Your Highness! Whenever you're ready, I'm ready!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! The relic's lit up again, and it's super bright this time!

choices.text: You want to go rafting again?
But haven't you already found your Guardian?

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: ...So we're all completely stumped.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Oh, it's you! Such a relief that you've come...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Thank you for coming, my honorable Paladin. We seem to have run into a rather peculiar problem...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Peculiar problem? Oh no, don't tell Paimon that the relic hasn't acknowledged Mr. Faurobert either?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: If the problem was only that I hadn't been acknowledged as Guardian, that would actually be simpler...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: How to put this... Mr. Faurobert is indeed the champion jumper — that much is indisputable.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But the trial he passed was Rainsong Pond's jumping contest, and when he was acknowledged as champion, it was a committee that declared him so.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: It is true that Her Highness resides in a tall tower, and that this kingdom does indeed have its own series of arduous trials...

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: But she clearly isn't trapped, much less needs me to jump up and rescue her.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: And those trials... No matter how good I was at jumping, I'd never be able to pass them... They just aren't designed for paper frogs.

choices.text: On paper, you seem like the perfect candidate...

response.speaker: Saborn
response.text: What are we to do...? If we can't complete our "calling"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You keep talking about this "calling" of yours, and Mr. Faurobert mentioned it too...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What exactly is it? If you haven't found the Guardian and princess you're looking for, why don't you just keep looking? Even if you don't find them right this instant, it's not like this place is gonna vanish into thin air...

response.speaker: Saborn
response.text: Our kingdom exists for its "calling"... It is also the only way we can save it.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Likewise, the residents of Rainsong Pond have sacrificed so much, and are continuing to sacrifice, for that princess who's nowhere to be found.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Generation after generation of champions have quietly aged away, all memory of their deeds fading away into oblivion...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Mr. Horellou has spoken of these brave ones before. Weighed down by the burden of unrealized ambition, they are left with no other choice but to end their days in obscurity. Such a fate is crueler than the fall of a kingdom.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Faurobert, we talked about this before. You said you were going to reconsider, and now...

choices.text: We must have faith in our champion.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: If I were perched on a lotus leaf and suddenly found myself drifting away with the current, I would do my best to make sure it didn't capsize in the middle of the river.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Now that I carry the Lotus Head Bangle, I will not... I cannot shirk my duty. This has nothing to do with courage, Mr. Horellou, just duty.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon knew our lotus leaf rafting experience wasn't a complete waste of time!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Spoken like a true champion!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: ...B—But if I do end up going overboard, you'll have to call for Estampe! He'd definitely be better at this than I am!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: *sigh* He's the real champion when it comes down to it, so why have I ended up being the one on the lotus leaf...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha... Looks like we still have to go rafting a few more times...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Ha, you sure are one unique champion. No matter how hard you try, you're always convinced you're going to fail.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: You really needn't worry. After all, not only did you come here entirely of your own accord, but you had the courage to shoulder a great responsibility.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: You were brave enough to make a choice and boldly follow through with it. At least in my eyes, you're no less than any flying squirrel.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Your Highness... Thank you for your praise, and for your trust. Besides, I'm already on this lotus leaf, so I can't get off now anyway.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Hahaha! Well anyway, now that we have the backing of so many strong fighters, I think it's high time we headed into the Cave of Eerie Murmurs to see what lurks in its depths.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Saborn, Souffache... There's no use trying to stop me. After all, when have you ever succeeded in holding me back?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Come on, lighten up! This is the last clue we need to save the kingdom.

response.speaker: Saborn
response.text: B—But... Not a single princess that's gone into the Cave of Eerie Murmurs has ever come back out again!

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If there's nothing in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs, what does it matter whether I return or not?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But on the other hand, if there really is a clue to the salvation of the kingdom in there, then even if I were to be trapped inside... That wouldn't be such a bad thing, would it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What kind of place is this Cave of Eerie Murmurs anyway? And why does Your Highness sound so serious?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Oh, it's nothing out of the ordinary. Simply put, it's where those princesses of past kingdoms searched for the "answer."

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But even until the day their kingdoms vanished utterly, those princesses were never seen again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? By "never seen again," surely you don't mean...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: There isn't a single flying squirrel that knows. But we'll find out soon enough.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: To be safe, I'll bring the relic along with us. Who knows, it might just come in handy.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Alright everyone, let's go. Given that one of you is an expert flyer, and the other a champion jumper, I trust you'll both be able to keep up with me?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Whoa, Her Highness has flown off already! Let's catch up, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: Our champion will not back down.
...But the details just didn't work out.
Looks like I'm here now, too.

talks.objective: Go to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Didn't the princess take us to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs before?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon's sure she heard a strange voice while we were there.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Uhm, just to let you guys know... Us paper frogs aren't very good at jumping in caves...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Mr. Faurobert! Paimon might've just been hearing things...
"...I am a voice, but a voice is not life..."
"...Interaction is only born of contradictions, and only interaction is dialogue..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There it is again!

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Do not fear, these voices will not harm us. They are simply lamenting their own past.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: To be precise, both princesses and princes. What they have in common is... They are all voices from fallen kingdoms.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: They came in search of answers, but found nothing. All they could do was stay and lament their fate in vain.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: You show great intuition, as one would expect of a Paladin. That is correct, I have come here often since my accession.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: After all, compared to all those princesses and princes from the past, there's nothing special about me at all.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: It was wishful thinking indeed for me to have imagined that a miracle might suddenly happen and that I'd find our true Guardian just like that.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But for the sake of my kingdom, I had to keep searching for a way to fulfill my "calling." I could not simply stand by and watch it fade away.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: So I looked everywhere, but found nothing. Finally, though, I narrowed down my search to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But because this cave has never been thoroughly investigated, and so as not to drive Saborn and Souffache sick with worry or cause their voices to go hoarse, I have never entered the Cave of Eerie Murmurs itself...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Now, for the future of the kingdom, and all our aged champions, I have no choice but to go in.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Don't be afraid, Your Highness! Not only do you have the super strong {NICKNAME} and the champion jumper Mr. Faurobert to back you up, but also the, uhh... seasoned floater Paimon, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #No matter what happens, we'll make sure you stay safe! Right, {NICKNAME}? Mr. Faurobert?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: W—We've... uh... G—Got your back? I think? I mean... We've hopefully got your back? Seriously, caves really aren't designed for jumping in...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: It's alright, Mr. Champion. We still have plenty of time to prepare.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: After all... We need to figure out how to get into this cave first.

choices.text: You must have come here many times before.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Lotus leaves and dewdrops, what the... Why has this story been carved on the wall?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Someone's carved a story here that goes: "Once upon a time, there was a paper frog who wished he had a pair of wings."

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: "He prayed to the goddess, who told him that if he could jump higher than all the other frogs, he would have his wings..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a sec... If he could already jump higher than all the other frogs, why would he need wings?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe it's just hyperbole.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: No... This champion's name is actually recorded in the committee's register.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: This paper frog, whose name was Cibrelus, once won the championship seven times in a row. No frog was his equal.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: His symbol was a pair of wings made of lotus leaves, so they dubbed him "Winged Cibrelus."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seven times in a row... P—Paimon heard you won the championship many times in a row, too, Mr. Faurobert...

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Me? Yes, I've won it seven times, and Estampe six.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: But I'd be no match for this champion! Back in those days, they had to figure it all out themselves, without any experience to go on.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: If my generation of frogs have jumped higher than others, it is merely by jumping up from the shoulders of giants...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There he goes again, putting himself down as usual...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So what happened to that champion?

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: This I do not know... According to the committee's records, in the last jumping contest he ever took part in, Cibrelus came second.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Second? So that means...

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Indeed it does. Given that he no longer felt up to the task of rescuing the princess, Cibrelus... announced his retirement there and then.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: He told his friend that the jumping contest no longer held any meaning for him, and that unless he rediscovered its meaning someday, he would never again compete.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: From that day forth, not once was his name ever again mentioned in the records of Rainsong Pond.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: ...So just like those princes and princesses, there was a point in time after which this champion simply vanished from the world.

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: That's right. *sigh* All in all, this story really doesn't seem like a promising omen...

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Hold on a minute... The last line of this story is also: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Why does this line keep reappearing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We'd better complete the rest of the trials first.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Yes, you're right. Let's focus on the puzzle before us.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: I wonder where it will lead us in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...What's all this in here?

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Looks like this cave has no intention of just giving us the answers, but rather plans on testing us instead...

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Hmm... The road to success is never straight, huh?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Thank you! Then let's... go take a look at this final trial!

choices.text: I'm a bit tired... I'll leave this one to you!

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: I am truly sorry to put you through all this, my Paladin. But this is the last step... Please, lend us your strength.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's so exhausted she feels like she can barely float...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But seeing as it's Her Highness asking, let's give it all we've got, {NICKNAME}.

talks.objective: Continue onward through the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Continue onward through the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's so chilly around here... Such a strange vibe...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's just glad we haven't seen anything weird...

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: ...Wait a sec, what's that carved on the wall over there?

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: It looks like... a story?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's it about?

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: "...After setting up the trial herself, the princess awaited her Guardian within the kingdom..."

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: I think I recall this story from the kingdom's records.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: In the legend, it is said that despite the passing of much time, still there came no sign of a Guardian, and it seemed that the kingdom's resources would soon run dry. The princess, whose name was Ceoya, therefore made a decision...

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: She let the kingdom's people fall into a deep slumber and sealed off all its land except the tower, where she alone remained to await the coming of the Guardian...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What became of this princess?

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: The Guardian that she awaited never came. In the end, she is said to have come to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs alone, then vanished from the world without a trace...

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: It is true that this princess showed great courage, but I cannot say that I agree with her approach.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: As I see it, by deciding to simply wait there while her people slept in blissful ignorance, she consigned her kingdom to an unknown fate.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Instead, she should have taken the initiative by calling upon her people to unite as one, seeking out this Guardian together.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: ...If she had done this, even if all their efforts had turned out to be in vain, at least she would have known that she'd done all she could.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Heh, it's just as the last line of the story says: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your Highness, it hasn't come to that yet...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, c'mon, there's still hope! And who knows, there might be some important clues left for us to find!

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Forgive me, I seem to have gotten a little carried away... Anyway, let's keep searching.

dialogues.speaker: Cimest
dialogues.text: Looking around, it seems like we haven't completed the trials in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs yet...

talks.objective: Continue onward through the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Continue onward through the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Try to complete the trial in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Oh, my leg... Is it still on the ground? I can barely feel it anymore.

choices.text: All four of your feet are still firmly on the ground, Mr. Champion.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...Those princesses from the past, they seem to have left, too. I hope that they'll never return to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, seems our trip to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs wasn't for nothing after all. With the relic lit up, there's hope for Your Highness's kingdom again.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: That is indeed so. The fact that the relic has lit up means that it has found a "Guardian" worthy of acknowledgment.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: It seems the "Guardian" that the relic was looking for was not a valiant warrior in the usual sense.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: A true "Guardian" who is worthy of acknowledgment is one who always follows their heart; someone who pushes forward relentlessly, in spite of their fear.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: It turns out that this relic, which we'd been treating like the problem, was actually the answer all along.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Those manuscripts that were waiting in the cave...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: They've been waiting for their path to appear... Waiting all this time.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But waiting leads only to more waiting. Hehe, no one can find the solution to a problem simply by searching within the problem itself.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Like... You wouldn't be able to pick a leaf from a tree if you were standing on the leaf itself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Sounds complicated. Paimon's feeling dizzy now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, none of them were acknowledged by the relic as Guardians. Your Highness and Mr. Faurobert were though!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So now the relic has lit up and we've found our Guardian, doesn't that mean that the problem's solved, Your Highness?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Well, you could say that. But I still haven't managed to figure out exactly why it lit up. Looks like Saborn and Souffache will be doing some more research for me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and now that the Guardian's been chosen, doesn't that mean that the relic's trial has lost its meaning, too?

choices.text: It'd be a shame to tear it all down.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: No, I will keep the trial in place. But it will now be used to "train" Guardians rather than to "choose" them.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If every flying squirrel were to become a Guardian someday, then no matter what difficulties the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells faced, we could overcome them together.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Hahaha, I've been wanting to do this for a long, long time. Just a pity that the relic refused to light up sooner, and that Saborn and Souffache stood in my way...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Now that I've been acknowledged by the relic, I shall do whatever I wish.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's why you're the princess, Your Highness!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nonono, Her Highness's title should now be... Guardian Princess of the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: So, umm... Your Highness, would it be alright if I, uhh, took part in the "training" in your kingdom?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: No, no... Didn't you hear that sound just now? That voice that was speaking?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: "...This is a trial that you must face, to serve Princess Cimest and fulfill your calling..."

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: It was the same as the voice of the manuscript that claimed to be Cibrelus in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Surely the great champion himself doesn't actually believe that I can fulfill Rainsong Pond's calling?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: But Princess Cimest doesn't need me to save her. If anything, I'm the one who needs her help...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you told him you could do it?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Huh? N—No, I didn't! Or rather, he had no intention of hearing my opinion anyway... But seeing as it's for the calling of Rainsong Pond, what choice do I have...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: You're saying you would like to undergo the trial? Then of course you're welcome to! I couldn't be more delighted to hear that the champion of Rainsong Pond is willing to serve in my kingdom.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Besides, I had plans to travel far away in the future, and I was actually just about to invite you to come along with me.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: After all, there are bound to be places in this world where the wind doesn't blow. When that time comes, we'll have to rely on those champion legs of yours.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Really? Th—Then I'll... try my best not to make any mistakes, though I've never tried jumping with anyone riding on my back before...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Then you'll have to train harder from now on. And to the two of you... Thank you for all the help you've given me and my kingdom.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Though there are still so many mysteries yet to be solved... Why did we need to find a Guardian, and why would a kingdom fall into decay by itself? And why would Rainsong Pond have such a calling...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But at least the kingdom has been saved, so now I have more time to contemplate these questions.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Sometimes, I can't help but think... That it would be best if this world really did have a "goddess" who wrote all the stories about us. That way, perhaps I would have a chance to ask her in person.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: But, Your Highness... Even if that goddess existed... Why would she write a story for us, but not an ending?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: First those poor souls in the cave, and now us. *sigh* We've all been through so much...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If that goddess did exist, I, too, would like to ask her. But regardless of whether or not she does, at least we learned that line.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...There are far too many matters on which I must deliberate more deeply. My loyal Paladin, please take these gifts as a token of my gratitude... These were the only treasures I brought with me.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If you have time, please come back to visit the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells again. I believe that... You may have some questions for me.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But first, I must... Rest well, and think hard.

choices.text: You're really up for anything now, huh...
I'd still like to have another go or two.
And they're in better condition than any of us are...

talks.objective: Try to complete the trial in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yay! That must mean we've passed this trial, huh? Hehe, that all went pretty smoothly.

choices.text: #Who's {M#king}{F#queen} of trials now? That's right, this {M#guy}{F#gal}.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: You're in such good shape! *sigh* If only I was as talented as you are...

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Huh? Did you hear that?
"Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."
"Once upon a time, there was a paper frog who wished he had a pair of wings."
"He prayed to the goddess, who told him that if he could jump higher than all the other frogs, he would have his wings..."
"Long ago, there was a princess who personally set up a trial in the kingdom..."
"She waited, and waited, and waited. O Guardian, where art thou..."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eek! The paper's talking!

response.speaker: Aged Manuscript
response.text: Another paper frog, just like me. Another useless champion, squandered years, and a pair of worthless, withered wings...

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: W—Wait, surely you can't be...

response.speaker: Aged Manuscript
response.text: I am an evaporated dewdrop, a pair of wings too weak for flight. The name "Cibrelus" is no longer one I am fit to bear.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: It is a great honor to meet you, Your Highness Princess Ceoya.

response.speaker: Exhausted Manuscript
response.text: It is an honor to meet you too, Your Highness. You, yet another stranger, another princess...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... Paimon's guessing they're the champion and princess mentioned in the story on the wall?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: They just look like two manuscripts...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: It is an honor to meet you both. You have resided in this cave for a long time now, so you should know why we are here.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Your Highness, have you found the answer you were looking for? Where is the Guardian we are looking for?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Great champion! Where is the princess that us paper frogs are supposed to save?

response.speaker: Aged Manuscript
response.text: ...You should go back. There are no answers here, only question after question.

response.speaker: Aged Manuscript
response.text: No river awaits, and the lotus leaves do not exist for us. The pond has never seen victory's laurel, nor a princess.

response.speaker: Aged Manuscript
response.text: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns"... Such a futile expectation. When will the cycle end...

response.speaker: Exhausted Manuscript
response.text: Keep waiting, keep waiting. There are no answers here, only question after question.

response.speaker: Exhausted Manuscript
response.text: The pen that wrote these words has not alighted back upon the page, yet the ink of fate has long dried up. Neither the Guardian nor the period that marks the end shall appear. Thus it has always been. Until now.

response.speaker: Exhausted Manuscript
response.text: "...But each should follow its own course." This is destiny's inexplicable hope. When will the path ahead reveal itself...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are they talking about? Paimon doesn't get it...

choices.text: Whatever it is, it doesn't sound too promising...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But why...

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: "No river awaits, and the lotus leaves do not exist for us." That makes it sound like Rainsong Pond is already...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: "Neither the Guardian nor the period that marks the end shall appear."

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Anyway, we shouldn't jump to conclusions too soon. We haven't even completed the trial yet.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: ...Alright. Giving up before the contest has even ended seems like bad etiquette indeed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's take care of the trials first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, let's stay positive! Maybe there'll be a pleasant surprise waiting for us!

choices.text: They might as well have said nothing.

talks.objective: Try to complete the trial in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Try to complete the trial in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, seems like we've passed all the trials, right?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...I brought the relic, but it hasn't reacted at all.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Are we really meant to just keep waiting here? But... What exactly are we waiting for?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's not like some kind of god's gonna suddenly swoop down and tell us what to do, is it?

response.speaker: Exhausted Manuscript
response.text: What we are willing to do... is wait. All we can do... is wait.

response.speaker: Aged Manuscript
response.text: Meaning lies in waiting; the future lies unknown.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When did they appear? And insisting that we wait like that... What are we even waiting for!?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Perhaps they do not know either. Which is why...

response.speaker: Aged Manuscript
response.text: We are echoes with nowhere to return, existences that do not exist, unfinished chapters of blank paper... As are you.

response.speaker: Exhausted Manuscript
response.text: Together, let us go back to where we belong. Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns... Each follows its own course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, you... piles of rotten paper! Why do you just keep telling us to wait!?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Pfft... Hahahaha! So that's it... I knew I wasn't in the wrong place.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Your Highness Princess Ceoya, I have my answer. To the rest of you — it is time for us to part ways.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Thank you all, for everything you have done. Now it is clear to me that the answer lies not in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: When I first arrived, I was afraid I would have to pay a heavy price to find a way to save the kingdom here.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: In the end, the Cave of Eerie Murmurs holds nothing more than a pile of old manuscripts deceiving themselves by waiting. It is a great relief to know that hope still lies elsewhere.

response.speaker: Exhausted Manuscript
response.text: ...The future lies unknown; meaning lies in waiting!

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: No, Your Highness. Meaning lies in the unknown.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Waiting leads only to waiting. I most certainly will not save the kingdom using such a method.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If the Guardian does not come, I will go in search of them. If I cannot find them in my kingdom, I will search the rest of the world instead.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If they are not to be found in this world, then I shall keep searching beyond it... Even if my kingdom is destined to fall, I wish to witness its final moments, when its ending is written.

response.speaker: Exhausted Manuscript
response.text: Such blindness, such impetuosity, such... frivolity!

response.speaker: Aged Manuscript
response.text: Such ignorance, such superficiality, such... impatience!

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Say what you will, but as you yourselves just put it: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If your path lies here in endless waiting, then mine lies instead on the road ahead.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Umm, c—can I say something? Uh... If you were to deem it acceptable, I would like to go along with Your Highness, too...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wow, someone seems pretty motivated all of a sudden!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: After all... If I could help Your Highness find your Guardian, that could also be interpreted as "saving the princess."

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: I am the champion of Rainsong Pond. Even if I do it for Rainsong Pond, I must continue to fulfill my duty...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If you are willing to help, then on behalf of the entire Kingdom of Breezes and Bells, I thank you.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: That is most alright! I will, of course, still have to ask the committee's opinion, especially Horellou and Estampe. As you know, I always seem to cause trouble...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! So what's ne...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Your Highness! Th—The relic next to you... It's lighting up!

choices.text: So long that they turned into manuscripts.

talks.objective: Try to complete the trial in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Leave the Cave of Eerie Murmurs
Leave the Cave of Eerie Murmurs

dialogues.speaker: Faurobert
dialogues.text: Oh, my leg... Is it still on the ground? I can barely feel it anymore.

choices.text: All four of your feet are still firmly on the ground, Mr. Champion.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...Those princesses from the past, they seem to have left, too. I hope that they'll never return to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, seems our trip to the Cave of Eerie Murmurs wasn't for nothing after all. With the relic lit up, there's hope for Your Highness's kingdom again.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: That is indeed so. The fact that the relic has lit up means that it has found a "Guardian" worthy of acknowledgment.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: It seems the "Guardian" that the relic was looking for was not a valiant warrior in the usual sense.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: A true "Guardian" who is worthy of acknowledgment is one who always follows their heart; someone who pushes forward relentlessly, in spite of their fear.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: It turns out that this relic, which we'd been treating like the problem, was actually the answer all along.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Those manuscripts that were waiting in the cave...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: They've been waiting for their path to appear... Waiting all this time.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But waiting leads only to more waiting. Hehe, no one can find the solution to a problem simply by searching within the problem itself.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Like... You wouldn't be able to pick a leaf from a tree if you were standing on the leaf itself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Sounds complicated. Paimon's feeling dizzy now...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyway, none of them were acknowledged by the relic as Guardians. Your Highness and Mr. Faurobert were though!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So now the relic has lit up and we've found our Guardian, doesn't that mean that the problem's solved, Your Highness?

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Well, you could say that. But I still haven't managed to figure out exactly why it lit up. Looks like Saborn and Souffache will be doing some more research for me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and now that the Guardian's been chosen, doesn't that mean that the relic's trial has lost its meaning, too?

choices.text: It'd be a shame to tear it all down.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: No, I will keep the trial in place. But it will now be used to "train" Guardians rather than to "choose" them.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If every flying squirrel were to become a Guardian someday, then no matter what difficulties the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells faced, we could overcome them together.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Hahaha, I've been wanting to do this for a long, long time. Just a pity that the relic refused to light up sooner, and that Saborn and Souffache stood in my way...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Now that I've been acknowledged by the relic, I shall do whatever I wish.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: That's why you're the princess, Your Highness!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nonono, Her Highness's title should now be... Guardian Princess of the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: So, umm... Your Highness, would it be alright if I, uhh, took part in the "training" in your kingdom?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: No, no... Didn't you hear that sound just now? That voice that was speaking?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: "...This is a trial that you must face, to serve Princess Cimest and fulfill your calling..."

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: It was the same as the voice of the manuscript that claimed to be Cibrelus in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs!

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Surely the great champion himself doesn't actually believe that I can fulfill Rainsong Pond's calling?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: But Princess Cimest doesn't need me to save her. If anything, I'm the one who needs her help...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So you told him you could do it?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Huh? N—No, I didn't! Or rather, he had no intention of hearing my opinion anyway... But seeing as it's for the calling of Rainsong Pond, what choice do I have...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: You're saying you would like to undergo the trial? Then of course you're welcome to! I couldn't be more delighted to hear that the champion of Rainsong Pond is willing to serve in my kingdom.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Besides, I had plans to travel far away in the future, and I was actually just about to invite you to come along with me.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: After all, there are bound to be places in this world where the wind doesn't blow. When that time comes, we'll have to rely on those champion legs of yours.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Really? Th—Then I'll... try my best not to make any mistakes, though I've never tried jumping with anyone riding on my back before...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Then you'll have to train harder from now on. And to the two of you... Thank you for all the help you've given me and my kingdom.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: Though there are still so many mysteries yet to be solved... Why did we need to find a Guardian, and why would a kingdom fall into decay by itself? And why would Rainsong Pond have such a calling...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But at least the kingdom has been saved, so now I have more time to contemplate these questions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Um... {NICKNAME}, don't you think that those manuscripts in the Cave of Eerie Murmurs seemed to be related to a story we heard before?

choices.text: That legend that Nilou told us about...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: D—Do you know something about all this?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it's a long and complicated... Well, actually, it's not that long or complicated a story...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Princess Cimest and Faurobert the story of the Goddess of Fate...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: So basically, everything we've been through... is a story written by the Goddess of Fate.

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: Alright... Now we've really become characters in a story. But seeing as that Goddess wrote us in, why didn't she give us an ending?

response.speaker: Faurobert
response.text: First those poor souls in the cave, and now us. *sigh* We've all been through so much...

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: So that must mean it was also the Goddess of Fate who came up with that line: "Stories follow rules, unfolding in cyclical patterns, but each should follow its own course."

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: ...I need some time to think about these matters more deeply. My loyal Paladin, please take these gifts as a token of my gratitude... These were the only treasures I brought with me.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: If you have time, please come back to visit the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells again. I believe that... You may have some questions for me.

response.speaker: Cimest
response.text: But first, I must... Rest well, and think hard.

choices.text: The Goddess of Fate who used ink to compose her stories...
You're really up for anything now, huh...
I'd still like to have another go or two.
And they're in better condition than any of us are...

dialogues.speaker: Saborn
dialogues.text: Honorable Guardian, what can I do for you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the kingdoms that failed to fulfill their calling...

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: You... Alright. Since the Princess herself has acknowledged you as the "Paladin of Breezes and Bells," it is only right that I tell you about such matters.

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: Prior to the current era of the Kingdom of Breezes and Bells, this land has known many kingdoms.

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: Just like us, their "calling" was to find a "Guardian of the Kingdom" who would be acknowledged by the relic.

dialogues.speaker: Saborn
dialogues.text: But these kingdoms, which were established to fulfill a "calling," declined and vanished before they could fulfill it.

dialogues.speaker: Saborn
dialogues.text: Not a single one of them managed to find a Guardian who could save the whole kingdom.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Vanished?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... If you can't fulfill this "calling" of yours, something bad will happen?

dialogues.speaker: Saborn
dialogues.text: That is correct. In some cases, the subjects of the kingdom suddenly lost their voices, while in others, the kingdom's water supply dried up overnight...

dialogues.speaker: Saborn
dialogues.text: Having lost their "future," all of these kingdoms eventually faded into oblivion.

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: If we cannot fulfill our "calling"... this will be our fate too.

dialogues.speaker: Souffache
dialogues.text: ...In any case, I wish you good luck, Paladin.

dialogues.speaker: Horellou
dialogues.text: Oh! Pleasure to meet you, hahaha! It seems you're a popular one indeed — even Her Highness Princess Cimest knows of you!

choices.text: About the "price" paid by Rainsong Pond...

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Oh... Such a heavy topic. Well, seeing as you've asked, it would be rude not to give you an answer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, but... Everything seems fine over at Rainsong Pond? You all look so happy to be jumping around and taking part in the contest...

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: In one sense, that is so. The waters of Rainsong Pond have never dried up, and the contest has never been interrupted.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Each committee working tirelessly away, and each contestant training constantly, doing everything they can to be up to the task of saving the princess someday.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: But all those paper frogs, endlessly laboring... They are the "price" that Rainsong Pond has paid.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: From the moment we are born, our "calling" is to practice jumping and save the princess... Every aspect of life at Rainsong Pond revolves around this.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Innumerable paper frogs have sat on Rainsong Pond's committee, and countless champions have been chosen... But all this time, we've never managed to find our princess.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Generation upon generation of frustrated champions have thus aged away, not knowing how to fulfill the "calling" that they so cherished...

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: All they can do is watch helplessly as their once powerful legs grow weak and their fine webbed feet gradually wither away.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Ha... And worst of all, because our champions keep aging, we must constantly train new ones to ensure that we have the strongest paper frogs ready at all times should the princess suddenly appear.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: So Rainsong Pond's contest continues without any sign of an ending. Yet now, none remember the names of those champions who — though they too once cherished the calling — ended up aging away in helpless impotence.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: As Princess Cimest put it, weighed down by the burden of unrealized ambition, they are left with no other choice but to end their days in obscurity. Such a fate is crueler than the fall of a kingdom.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: But that's enough about all that! The atmosphere's suddenly feeling rather heavy. Let us place our trust in Faurobert and Princess Cimest — I'm sure they'll be able to do something about it.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Oh, that good fellow? He said he was going for a stroll to get some fresh air. Perhaps he's practicing his diving as we speak.

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: *sigh* If only Estampe could share some of his relaxed mindset with Faurobert. Even a fifth of it would do...

response.speaker: Horellou
response.text: Alright, please take care. I'll be waiting here for you all to return.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: [Timeline: The relic lights up, the current takes form, the lamp flies in, the player walks over to the current]
